# Foundation for Economic Education (FEE)

> > The Foundation for Economic Education (FEE) is a leading educational organization promoting classical liberal ideas, free-market economics, and individual liberty through articles, research, and student programs.

FEE publishes analysis on economic policy, history, and philosophy from scholars worldwide, covering topics from tariffs and trade to entrepreneurship and institutional economics. The organization offers educational workshops and maintains transparent financial reporting as a nonprofit dedicated to economic education.

## Key Topics

- Free-market economics
- Classical liberalism
- Economic history
- Government intervention
- Trade and tariffs
- Welfare state analysis
- Price controls
- Economic growth
- Austrian School economics
- Entrepreneurship education
- Public vs. private education
- Institutional economics
- Nonprofit transparency
- Adam Smith
- Liberty and individual rights

## Current Economic Policy Analysis

- [Trump's Credit Card Rate Cap](https://fee.org/articles/trumps-credit-card-rate-cap): Louis Rouanet analyzes Trump's 10% credit card interest rate cap proposal
- [Trump's Tariffs in Trouble](https://fee.org/articles/trumps-tariffs-in-trouble): Supreme Court challenges to Trump's IEEPA-based tariff authority
- [The Intellectual Foundations of Protectionism](https://fee.org/articles/the-intellectual-foundations-of-protectionism): Hamilton and List's infant industry argument for trade protectionism
- [AI's Energy Appetite](https://fee.org/articles/ais-energy-appetite): Google Gemini's energy consumption and nuclear power for AI data centers
- [Deepfakes and the Digital Wild West](https://fee.org/articles/deepfakes-and-the-digital-wild-west): Denmark's copyright law expansion to combat AI deepfakes and identity theft

## Economic History and Theory

- [Carl Menger: Ivory Tower Iconoclast](https://fee.org/articles/carl-menger-ivory-tower-iconoclast): Austrian School founder Carl Menger's economic contributions and legacy
- [The Drivers of Prosperity](https://fee.org/articles/the-drivers-of-prosperity): Lonis Hamaili on Britain's Industrial Revolution and economic growth drivers
- [A Forgotten Classical Liberal in Mexico](https://fee.org/articles/a-forgotten-classical-liberal-in-mexico): Francisco Zarco's classical liberal legacy in 19th-century Mexico
- [Latin America's Lag](https://fee.org/articles/latin-americas-lag): Pedro Urso on institutional economics and Latin American underdevelopment

## Welfare State and Government Programs

- [Intergenerational Plunder](https://fee.org/articles/intergenerational-plunder): France and Britain's pension systems as intergenerational fiscal traps
- [#52-Progressives Have Good Intentions, So What Else is Required?](https://fee.org/articles/52-progressives-have-good-intentions-so-what-else-is-required): Lawrence Reed on progressive intentions vs welfare state outcomes
- ['Democratic Socialism': Yet Another Remake](https://fee.org/articles/democratic-socialism-yet-another-remake): Julieta Clara's Argentine perspective on democratic socialism failures
- [The Czech Republic's Stand Against Communism](https://fee.org/articles/the-czech-republics-stand-against-communism): Czech Republic's anti-communist laws and historical memory in Prague

## Education and Markets

- [#51 – The Free Market Cannot Provide Public Education](https://fee.org/articles/51-the-free-market-cannot-provide-public-education): Sheldon Richman on free market education vs government schooling
- [Bureaucracy, Conformity, and Mediocrity](https://fee.org/articles/bureaucracy-conformity-and-mediocrity): Lika Kobeshavidze critiques Europe's free university bureaucracy model
- [Revolution of One Unleash Your Inner Entrepreneur](https://fee.org/classroom-2/revolution-of-one-unleash-your-inner-entrepreneur): FEE's entrepreneurial education workshops for students with T.K. Coleman

## About FEE

- [Financial Data](https://fee.org/about/financial-data): FEE's financial transparency data including IRS Form 990 and audits

## Optional

- [Black Friday and Giving Tuesday: True Free-Market 'Holidays'](https://fee.org/articles/black-friday-and-giving-tuesday-true-free-market-holidays): Black Friday and Giving Tuesday as voluntary free-market phenomena
- [Wimbledon vs. The Super Bowl](https://fee.org/articles/wimbledon-vs-the-super-bowl): Economics of tennis prize money compared to NFL Super Bowl revenue
- [Ex-Google VP on the 'One Skill' She Looked For at Job Interviews Above All Others—That Only 15% of People Have](https://fee.org/articles/ex-google-vp-on-the-one-skill-she-looked-for-at-job-interviews-above-all-others-that-only-15-of-people-have): Claire Hughes Johnson on self-awareness as key hiring trait at Google
